page: Microsoft Azure F16-8amds_v7 is a constrained-core virtual machine configuration based on AMD EPYC 9V45 processors operating at up to 4.5 GHz. Built on Microsoft Hyper-V and the x86_64 architecture, this instance allocates 8 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core. Memory provision is substantial at 128 GB of RAM, offering a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16 GB per core. The server includes 1888 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and no GPU hardware is attached.

Benchmark data highlights exceptional single-thread performance, driven by high core clocks and AMD Zen-based architectural enhancements like AVX-512 vector extensions. In synthetic testing, stress-ng single-core performance reached 3730.67 points, placing in the top decile. Similarly, single-threaded gzip compression hit 40.74 GB/s and bzip3 decompression delivered 18.08 GB/s, both ranking in the top 10 percent. Multi-threaded metrics reflect the 8-core allocation, showing middle-tier throughput with a multi-core stress-ng score of 29555.44 and PassMark CPU score of 24491.61. Small-scale language model inference demonstrates notable efficiency for a CPU deployment, producing 369.42 tokens per second on 135M parameter models.

The constrained-core layout delivers high memory density and NVMe capacity per core, optimizing per-core software licensing costs. While multi-threaded throughput is constrained by the 8-core limit compared to larger instances, workloads requiring substantial cache, high memory ceilings, fast scratch storage, and robust single-thread compute benefit efficiently. Microsoft Azure F16-8amds_v7 is well suited for memory-bound relational databases, in-memory caching systems such as Redis, batch decompression jobs, and data pipeline ETL workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure F16-8amds_v7 is an AMD EPYC 9V45 virtual machine providing 8 dedicated physical cores at clock speeds up to 4.5 GHz on Microsoft Hyper-V. It features 128 GB of RAM, equating to 16 GB per core, coupled with 1888 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and zero GPUs. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier single-threaded performance, including top-decile stress-ng single-core execution and gzip compression at 40.74 GB/s. Multi-core compute and PassMark database operations place in the median range due to the constrained 8-core footprint. This configuration offers high resource density per core, making it an efficient option for licensing models tied to CPU count. It is suitable for memory-intensive relational databases, Redis caching, compression tasks, and analytics workloads that demand large memory footprints and local NVMe storage without excessive core counts.
